answer: kappa = 2^-182 is half of the smallest margin in the cost accounting; it is not a free choice. After dividing every cost by V = Theta(n), each of the seven dominant costs is a power p^(1-g_i), where the margin g_i is one minus the exponent. The smallest margin is g_2 = eps*c*(1-tau), which belongs to the chunk exchanges (the p K^(tau-1) term): 2^-75 * 2^-56 * 2^-50 = 2^-181 = 2*kappa. So every dominant term is at most p^(1-2*kappa). Any fixed power of log p is at most p^kappa eventually, so the normalized total is O(p^(1-kappa)) and the time is O(n (lg n)^(1-kappa)). The margin is 2*kappa because one kappa of it is spent absorbing the log factors and the remaining kappa is the saving. The pages do not argue why exactly half is taken; the constants eps, c, tau and lambda' are called conservative without justification.

reason: Answered, with reasonable confidence. The arithmetic checks: g_2 = 2^-75 * 2^-56 * 2^-50 = 2^-181 = 2*kappa, and the pages state the bookkeeping (dominant terms at most p^(1-2*kappa), log factors absorbed by p^kappa, total p^(1-kappa)). Less sure of: why exactly half is taken (the pages do not argue it); why the constants are conservative; and the source of the O(p/K) chunk-exchange count for the layout, which the Lolazad page does not show.
